def:demand-profile:
Definition Demand profile of a derived atom. Let \mathcal{A}(Z, N) = \sum_w c_w \cdot w be a derived atom in normal form. Its demand profile is

  \mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A})
  \;=\;
  \{(w, c_w) : c_w < 0\}
  \;\subset\;
  \mathrm{NF}(B_A) \times \mathbb{R}_{<0}.

The demand magnitude is |\mathrm{dem}| = \sum_{c_w < 0} |c_w|.
prop:demand-stability:
Proposition Demand profile determines nuclear and atomic stability. The derived atom \mathcal{A}(Z, N) is:

  1. Beta-stable if and only if, for all single nucleon exchanges \mathfrak{p} \leftrightarrow \mathfrak{n} at fixed A = Z + N:
  |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z, N))|
  \;\leq\;
  |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z \pm 1, N \mp 1))|.

The stable configuration minimizes the demand magnitude at fixed A.

  1. Shell-closed if and only if \mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}) = \varnothing. All NF coefficients are non-negative.
  2. Doubly magic if both the nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) and the atom \mathcal{A}(Z, N) have locally minimal Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M among neighboring (Z, N).

The demand-free {}^3\mathrm{He} and the Markov-trace-minimal {}^4\mathrm{He} represent two distinct stability mechanisms: shell closure (zero demand) and action minimization (lowest trace).
prop:nuclear-operator-regimes:
Proposition Three operator regimes for nuclear binding. In the inductive construction of \mathcal{N}(Z, N), the inter-nucleon binding operator \Phi_k selected at step k for the nuclei recorded in this chapter belongs to one of three regimes:

(Regime I — Shell filling.) At the first step of the first nuclear shell, the selected operator is the five-crossing three-strand braid

  \Phi_k = (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2\sigma_0
  \qquad (k = 1,\; p \to pp),

whose closure is the T(2,4) torus link.

(Regime II — Magic shell closure.) At and immediately after a magic number, the selected operator is L_\pm (closure in B_3: the unknot):

  \Phi_k \in \{L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1,\; L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0\}

The L_\pm operators, whose closures are the unknot, achieve demand closure at magic shell boundaries.

(Regime III — Open shell.) Beyond a closed magic shell, the selected operator reverts to the bare typed crossing:

  \Phi_k \in \{C_{pp},\; C_{pn},\; C_{nn}\}

The operator transitions from (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2\sigma_0 to L_+ at the first magic number, then to L_- at the shell boundary, and finally to C_{pn} in the open shell. The \mathcal{B}_3 Borromean operator is not selected at any recorded nuclear step; it appears only as the quark-level confinement operator.
rem:nuclear-operator-regimes-interpretat:
Remark Physical interpretation of the three nuclear binding regimes. The three operator regimes carry this physical interpretation:

  • Regime I (torus knot): Initial nucleons interact as individual particles. The residual strong force between them forms the cinquefoil T_{2,5}.
  • Regime II (Hopf link): At magic numbers, the filled shell acts collectively. A new nucleon crosses the entire shell rather than individual nucleons. This collective Hopf link binds the new nucleon, driving shell closure.
  • Regime III (bare crossing): Beyond the magic shell, the nucleus is large enough that new nucleons interact via simple pairwise crossings. The existing normal form already encodes the collective effects.
rem:nuclear-regimes-shadow-price-kinks-p: Remark Prior art for toric chamber flips, magic-shell shadow-price kinks, and finite-nucleon phase walls. The regime transitions in Three operator regimes for nuclear binding and the integer cluster assembly in Physical cluster chamber, drip-line monomer reduction, and the Hoyle triple-alpha bottleneck realize a sharp geometric mechanism that connects combinatorial optimization, density-functional theory, and nuclear shell physics.
rem:periodic-table-demand:
Remark The valley of stability is the demand-minimizing locus in (Z, N)-space. Conjecture. For each mass number A = Z + N, the experimentally observed stable isotope (Z_*, N_*) is the unique minimizer of the demand magnitude:

  (Z_*, N_*)
  =
  \arg\min_{Z + N = A}
  |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z, N))|

where \mathcal{A}(Z, N) is the derived atom (derived atom) and |\mathrm{dem}| is the demand magnitude (demand stability).
sec:derived-atoms-intro:
To verify how the three operator regimes of Nuclear Binding Regimes and Magic Numbers operate on concrete braid words, this section computes the explicit Gröbner–Shirshov normal forms and Markov-trace binding energies for five benchmark light nuclei:

  • Hydrogen (^1\mathrm{H}): The single-nucleon base case with zero inter-nucleon crossings.
  • Deuterium (^2\mathrm{H}): The minimal two-nucleon bound braid in the T = 0 isospin-singlet channel, whose Markov-trace volume integral yields a zero-parameter binding prediction against AME 2020.
  • Helium-4 (^4\mathrm{He}): The first doubly magic closure (Z = N = 2), where the two-row Wedderburn stratum saturates.
  • Lithium-6 (^6\mathrm{Li}) and Oxygen-16 (^{16}\mathrm{O}): The post-magic transition at A = 6 and the second doubly magic closure at Z = N = 8, providing the normal-form data consumed by the typed Garside staircase construction in Typed Garside Element and Gram-Weighted \mathcal{Q}_q-Value.

sec:garside-gram-intro:
The light-nucleus normal forms of Derived Light-Atom Normal Forms exhibit a recurring staircase pattern of typed proton and neutron crossings. This section formalizes that pattern by defining the typed Garside element \Delta_{Z,N} of the nuclear braid and expressing the reaction \mathcal{Q}_q-value as a Gram-inverse weighted Frobenius norm over conversion channels.

At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the Frobenius Gram matrix G on the full Hecke algebra H_n(q) has a non-trivial radical equal to the kernel of the Temperley–Lieb projection (y_{(1^3)} = 0), so the inverse-Gram weighting G^{-1} is evaluated on the non-degenerate quotient H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad}\,G \cong \mathrm{TL}_n(q). Proving that the Gram eigenstructure coincides with the adjoint character on the surviving Wedderburn blocks anchors the \mathcal{Q}_q-value in the Jucys–Murphy spectral data and prepares the transfer-matrix factorisation of Transfer Matrices and Beta-Decay Transitions.
def:typed-garside-element:
Definition Typed Garside element of the nuclear braid. Let \mathcal{A}(Z, N) be a nucleus with A = Z + N nucleons in ordering (t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1}) where t_i \in \{p, n\}. The typed Garside element is the element \mathcal{G}(t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1}) \in H_A(q) built by the Garside staircase with typed crossings.

Construction. The Garside staircase has A - 1 levels. At level \ell, strand \ell + 1 crosses all earlier strands from right to left. Each crossing is typed by the nucleon pair (t_j, t_{\ell+1}):

\begin{equation}\label{eq:typed-garside}
  \mathcal{G}(t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1})
  \;=\;
  \prod_{\ell=0}^{A-2}
  \;\prod_{j=\ell}^{0}
  C(t_j,\, t_{\ell+1};\, \sigma_j),
\end{equation}

where C(f_i, f_j; \sigma_k) = \sigma_k + d(f_i, f_j) is the typed crossing operator with coefficients:

  d(p, p) = 0, \qquad
  d(n, n) = -(q - q^{-1}), \qquad
  d(p, n) = d(n, p) = -\tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}).

The result is reduced to Gröbner–Shirshov normal form under the braiding-induced ordering.
rem:typed-garside-element-adjacent-compa: Remark Comparison with the adjacent-only construction. Comparison with adjacent-only construction. The transfer matrix chain computes vertex volumes at each generator by chaining the crossing coefficients. This captures the same pairwise crossing data as the Garside staircase, but factored through scalar vertex volumes rather than the full H_A(q) element. The typed Garside element retains the complete algebraic structure.
prop:gram-weighted-qvalue:
Proposition Gram-weighted \mathcal{Q}_q-value from Frobenius norm of conversion channels.

Scope. Three auxiliary properties in this block are stated as open hypotheses: that \Delta_k > 0, that the Gram weights favour boundary neutrons, and that G is indefinite. Treat them as open.

Let \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} = \mathcal{G}(t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1}) be the typed Garside element of the parent nucleus in H_A(q). Let G be the Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) restricted to the NF subspace spanned by \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} and all conversion daughters. The Q-value for \beta^- decay is:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:gram-weighted-qvalue}
  Q(Z, N)
  \;=\;
  \biggl(
    \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
    w_k^G \;\cdot\; \Delta_k
  \biggr)
  \,\times\, N \,\times\, m_e
\end{equation}

where:

  1. The sum runs over all N neutrons in the parent.
  2. \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dau}}^{(k)} is the typed Garside element of the daughter obtained by converting neutron k, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nf-reduction-cost}
  \Delta_k
  \;=\;
  \lVert \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} \rVert_1
  \;-\;
  \lVert \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dau}}^{(k)} \rVert_1
\end{equation}

is the NF reduction cost.

  1. The Gram weight for neutron k is:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gram-weight}
  w_k^G
  \;=\;
  \frac{
    \lVert \delta_k \rVert_F
  }{
    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \lVert \delta_j \rVert_F
  },
  \qquad
  \delta_k
  \;=\;
  \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} - \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dau}}^{(k)},
  \qquad
  \lVert \delta_k \rVert_F
  \;=\;
  \sqrt{|\delta_k \cdot G \cdot \delta_k|}
\end{equation}

where \lVert \cdot \rVert_F is the Frobenius norm induced by the Gram matrix.

Inputs. The substrate parameter q and the electron mass m_e. There are no other parameters.
rem:gram-weight-eigenstructure: Remark Eigenstructure of the Gram weight and the adjoint character. The Gram weights w_k^G arise from the eigenstructure of the Gram matrix G on H_A(q). They reflect the decomposition of H_A(q) into irreducible representations.
sec:transfer-beta-decay-intro:
Equipped with the Gram-weighted \mathcal{Q}_q-value on the Temperley–Lieb quotient, \beta-decay transitions admit a compact operator representation. Because the nuclear skein polynomial factors as a product of 2 \times 2 transfer matrices along the braid word, converting a neutron strand into a proton strand corresponds to inserting a single transition matrix into the universal transfer-matrix product.

This section records how nucleon-ordering ansatzes behave under \Phi_q (noting that for A \geq 4 the interleaved tail-packed ansatz does not generally minimise \Phi_q), derives symbolic closed forms for the free-neutron decay Q-value and the normal-form counit transition, and proves exponential convergence of the trace-counit expansion toward the pre-archimedean difference \Delta_{\mathrm{pre}}. It then examines the relation between the counit formulation and the transfer-matrix log-ratio formulation (Form B) of the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta spectral bridge.

rem:energy-scale-planck: Remark Energy scale E_0 and the Planck time. The energy scale E_0 is derived from CAL-1 (m_e) and CAL-2 (q_0) alone. It consumes no \beta-decay calibration. It has a natural interpretation in terms of the q-deformed Planck scale: it represents the energy of one Hecke reduction step. This is the physical cost of resolving a single \sigma_i^2 \to h\sigma_i + \mathbf{1}.
prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic: Proposition Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay. Conditional on Borromean quark conjecture. The Q-value of free neutron \beta^--decay n \to p + e^- + \bar\nu_e is derived symbolically from the categorical three-calibration inputs m_e (H^0) and q_0 (H^1). The value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(n) (H^2) is the \beta-decay datum being predicted, not used as input.
prop:qbeta-counit-closed-form:
Proposition Closed form of the counit Q-value \varepsilon(\Delta)\cdot\mathfrak{E}_0. Let \Delta = \mathrm{NF}(n) - \mathrm{NF}(p) be the single-wrap normal-form difference of the neutron and proton typed-crossing elements in H_3(q), and write h = q - q^{-1}. Let \varepsilon denote the coordinate-sum functional \sigma \mapsto 1 (see the scope section below — it is not a counit) and \mathfrak{E}_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)) the per-Hecke-step energy scale. Then:

  \varepsilon(\Delta)\cdot\mathfrak{E}_0
  \;=\;
  \frac{m_e\,(q+1)(q^2 - 2q - 1)}{2q^3}.
rem:qbeta-counit-transition: Remark \mathfrak{Q}_\beta as a counit transition observable. The closed form clarifies the standing of the free-neutron relation \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = |\Delta(\mathrm{net})|\cdot\mathfrak{E}_0. The relation uses the Frobenius counit \varepsilon, whereas the per-braid mass uses the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M.
conj:qbeta-trace-counit-convergence:
Conjecture Trace–counit convergence of the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta mass difference. The per-braid Markov-trace nucleon mass difference \mathfrak{m}(n) - \mathfrak{m}(p) - m_e, summed over the brane tower, equals the Frobenius-counit Q-value \varepsilon(\Delta)\cdot\mathfrak{E}_0:

  \mathfrak{m}(n) - \mathfrak{m}(p) - m_e
  \;=\;
  \varepsilon(\Delta)\cdot\mathfrak{E}_0
  \;=\;
  \frac{m_e\,(q+1)(q^2 - 2q - 1)}{2q^3}.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, and numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prop:delta-pre-archimedean:
Proposition Difference observables are formed pre-archimedean: fold commutes with the delta, the archimedean realisation does not. Let f be any fibre fold. Since f is an additive map on the fibre coefficient ring, for any fibre quantities x_{\mathfrak n}, x_{\mathfrak p}:

  f\bigl(x_{\mathfrak n} - x_{\mathfrak p}\bigr)
  \;=\; f(x_{\mathfrak n}) - f(x_{\mathfrak p}).

By contrast, the archimedean realisation \tau is a nonlinear \mathrm{Li}_2^q-tower. Thus, in general:

  \tau(x_{\mathfrak n}) - \tau(x_{\mathfrak p})
  \;\neq\; \tau\bigl(x_{\mathfrak n} - x_{\mathfrak p}\bigr).
sec:transfer-beta-decay-q-beta-spectral-: The second half of the transfer-matrix analysis connects the algebraic counit expansion to the spectral-bridge log-ratio \ln(V_{pp}/V_{nn}). This subsection proves the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta spectral-bridge proposition and the exponential decay bound on the archimedean remainder, evaluates the depth-1 symbolic closed forms, and proves the vanishing of the \beta-decay amplitude at the silver-ratio fixed point. It concludes by relating normal-form observability and negative-deficit confinement to the physical MeV scale E_0 = m_e/\bigl(q_0(q_0-1)(1-\hbar_q^2)\bigr) and the T_{3,5} braid transition visualizer.
conj:q-beta-spectral-bridge:
Conjecture \mathfrak{Q}_\beta spectral bridge: Form A (NF counit) and Form B (transfer-matrix log-ratio) are the same observable in different bases. Conditional on Borromean quark conjecture.

Let \mathcal{B}_n be the canonical free-neutron braid word with single wrap A = 1. Let q = q_0 be the substrate parameter and h := q - q^{-1}. Define the Markov–Jones parameter as:

  z \;:=\; \frac{q^{3}}{q^{2}+1} \;=\; \frac{q^{2}}{[2]_q}.

Write E_0 := m_e/(q(q-1)) for the single-tick energy scale. Let:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}} \;:=\;
  \lvert \Delta(\mathrm{net}) \rvert \cdot E_0
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}} \;:=\;
  \ln\!\frac{V_{\mathrm{pp}}}{V_{\mathrm{nn}}} \cdot \frac{E_0}{z}

denote the closed-form Q-value in the normal form counit basis and the transfer-matrix eigenfunction basis, respectively. Both forms are finite-depth truncations of the same spectral decomposition. They agree as:

  \frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}}}
  \;=\;
  1 \;+\; \frac{(z-1)\,h}{2} \;+\; O(h^2),

with bridge identity:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}}
  \;=\;
  \ln\!\frac{V_{\mathrm{pp}}}{V_{\mathrm{nn}}} \cdot \frac{E_0}{z}
  \cdot \Bigl(1 + \tfrac{(z-1)\,h}{2} + O(h^2)\Bigr).

The remainder at depth N in the brane-tower truncation decays exponentially.

rem:q-beta-spectral-bridge-sketch:
Remark Argument sketch for the Q_β spectral bridge. Sketch.

Scope of the asymptotic expansion. Two sub-steps in the Taylor comparison are conditional: First, the order-h^2 term of \ln(V_{\mathrm{pp}}/V_{\mathrm{nn}}): the step z h + O(h^2) = \ln(1 + zh) + O(h^3) needs the h^2 coefficient to be -z^2/2, which is not computed. Second, the exponential remainder rests on conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-decay, a conjecture, so the remainder bound is conditional. The +1.31 keV residual and the CODATA 7\% agreement are empirical comparisons, not proof steps.

Form A side. The normal form counit reads \lvert\Delta(\mathrm{net})\rvert = h(2 - h)/2 = h - h^2/2 + O(h^3), obtained via direct expansion of the single-wrap symbolic closed form (prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic).

Form B side. The Hecke perturbation carries the half-factor \Delta_\beta(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})\,\mathbb{I} = \tfrac{h}{2}\,\mathbb{I} (prop:beta-decay-transfer-matrix). The change in Markov-traced volume per generator incorporates this factor:

  \Delta \hat V_i
  \;=\;
  z\,(\Delta M_i)_{11} + (\Delta M_i)_{21}
  \;=\;
  \tfrac{z\,h}{2} + O(h^2).

At single wrap with A = 1, the proton-to-neutron conversion affects two generators, \sigma_0 and \sigma_1 (prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic). The total log-ratio is:

  \ln\!\frac{V_{\mathrm{pp}}}{V_{\mathrm{nn}}}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i \in \{0,1\}}
    \ln\!\frac{\hat V^{\mathrm{pp}}_i}{\hat V^{\mathrm{nn}}_i}
  \;\approx\;
  2 \cdot \tfrac{z\,h}{2}
  \;=\;
  z\,h \;+\; O(h^2)
  \;=\;
  \ln(1 + z\,h) + O(h^3).

Ratio. Form the dimensionless ratio \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}} / \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}} and divide by E_0 to cancel h in the leading term:

\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}}}
&=
\frac{h - h^2/2 + O(h^3)}
     {(z h - z^2 h^2 / 2 + O(h^3))\,/\,z} \\
&=
\frac{h - h^2/2}{h - z h^2 / 2} \cdot \bigl(1 + O(h)\bigr) \\
&=
\frac{1 - h/2}{1 - z h/2} \cdot \bigl(1 + O(h)\bigr) \\
&= 1 + \tfrac{(z - 1)\,h}{2} + O(h^2).
\end{aligned}

The intermediate identity \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}}/E_0 \cdot z = z h - (z h)^2/2 + O(h^3) isolates the dimensional content of the 1/z factor. Form B requires z to normalize the eigenfunction basis to the Markov-traced volume. This does not mean that Form A and Form B measure different observables.

Exponential remainder. Both truncations inhabit the spectral decomposition of the q-Hamiltonian along the Gröbner basis filtration of the free-neutron sector K \subset H_3(q) at q = q_0. Following conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-decay, each finite-depth truncation \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(N)} incurs an error bounded by C(K) \cdot e^{-c(K) N}, where C, c > 0 are structural constants. At N = 0, this yields the observed +1.31 keV residual. At N \geq 1, the bound is sub-keV.
conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-d:
Conjecture Exponential decay of the archimedean brane-tower truncation remainder. Fix a free-neutron sector K \subset H_3(q). Let \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(N)} be the depth-N brane-tower truncation of the \beta-decay Q-value. Let \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{exact}} be the value of the full spectral decomposition. Then there exist constants C(K), c(K) > 0 such that the truncation remainder R_N(K) \;:=\; \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(N)} - \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{exact}} decays exponentially in the truncation depth:

  \bigl\lvert R_N(K) \bigr\rvert
  \;\le\;
  C(K)\,e^{-c(K)\,N}
  \qquad (N \ge 0).

prop:silver-ratio-beta-decay-null:
Proposition Silver-ratio trace degeneracy: at q = 1 \pm \sqrt{2}, the Hecke generator \sigma has eigenvalues = 1 \pm \sqrt{2} (silver-ratio self-referential fixed point); proton and neutron Markov-traces become categorically indistinguishable. Let q be the substrate parameter, h = q - q^{-1} the Hecke skein parameter, and \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) = h/2 the per-crossing energy. Then:

\boxed{\;
\Delta(\mathrm{net})
\;=\;
\frac{h(h-2)}{2}
\;=\;
\frac{(q^2-1)(q^2 - 2q - 1)}{2q^2}
\;=\;
2\,\mathfrak{E}_\times\!\left(\mathfrak{E}_\times - 1\right)
\;}

vanishes if and only if h \in \{0, 2\}, equivalently if and only if

\mathfrak{E}_\times \in \{0, 1\},

that is, if and only if each crossing carries either zero or unit energy. The two roots are q = 1 (undeformed substrate, \mathfrak{E}_\times = 0) and q = 1 + \sqrt{2}, the silver mean (unit crossing energy); the conjugate root q = 1 - \sqrt{2} is negative and outside the substrate range.

The crossing-energy form is equivalent to the h-form by \mathfrak{E}_\times = h/2. Its roots \{0, 1\} are the fixed points of x \mapsto x^2.

At q = 1 + \sqrt{2}:

  1. The Hecke quadratic \sigma^2 = h\sigma + 1 becomes \sigma^2 = 2\sigma + 1. The generator \sigma has eigenvalues equal to the silver-ratio conjugates themselves.
  2. Proton and neutron single-wrap Markov traces become equal: \mathrm{net}(p) = \mathrm{net}(n) = 1 - h/2 = 1 - \mathfrak{E}_\times = 0.

Behaviour of the mass formula at the two roots. The volume term carries \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} in the denominator as \mathrm{Vol}/\hbar_q^{2}. At \mathfrak{E}_\times = 0, i.e. q = 1, that denominator is zero. At \mathfrak{E}_\times = 1 it equals (1 - (1+\sqrt2)^{-1})^2 = 0.343\ldots, and item 2 above states that the trace does not separate proton from neutron there.

Relation to the volume conjecture. The volume-conjecture limit is taken at roots of unity q = e^{2\pi i/N}, for which |q| = 1, whereas \mathfrak{E}_\times = 1 gives |q| = 1 + \sqrt{2}. The limit in which the volume term equals the hyperbolic volume is q \to \infty, where \hbar_q \to 1 and \mathrm{Vol}/\hbar_q^{2} \to \mathrm{Vol}.
rem:silver-ratio-beta-decay-null-interpr: Remark Silver-ratio bar-symmetry, \mathrm{SU}(2)_L connection, and the c_5 outlier. The null at h = 2 is the unique value where the bar-anti-symmetric kernel vanishes inside the empirical kinematic window.

rem:beta-decay-energy-scale:
Remark Energy scale of the Hecke normal form: from dimensionless debt to MeV. The Gröbner--Shirshov normal form coefficients are dimensionless Laurent polynomials in q. To connect them to observed energies, an energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 (in MeV) is needed such that:

  |\Delta(\mathrm{net})| \times \mathfrak{E}_0
  = 
  Q_{\beta}
  = 
  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} - \mathfrak{m}_{e}
   \approx  0.7823 \text{MeV}.

The framework provides \mathfrak{E}_0 in two forms. The first is a single-Planck-tick (N=0) value. The second is a tower-summed geometric form. These differ by the brane-tower correction 1/(1-\hbar_q^2) \approx 1.0099. Both derive from CAL-1 (m_e) and CAL-2 (q_0) alone.
rem:negative-debt-confinement: Remark Negative coefficient debt, confinement, and the nine-strand direction. The NF_+ / NF_- decomposition of the nucleon normal forms reveals a quantitative signature of confinement. The neutron carries significantly more internal cancellation than the proton.
